units.title: Primary health care is broader than one clinic
units.lesson: WHO describes primary health care as a whole-of-society approach. It combines integrated services, action on wider determinants and empowered people and communities. It spans promotion, prevention and care across the life course. Primary care services are a central part, but the broader approach also includes public health and cross-sector action.
units.question: Which best describes primary health care in WHO’s framework?
choices: Only one hospital building
A whole-of-society approach including services and wider determinants
Only a private billing system
units.explanation: The framework includes services, determinants and community participation.
rationales: A building alone is too narrow.
This captures the broader approach.
Billing is not the framework.

units.title: Know what NOHP aims to strengthen
units.lesson: India’s National Oral Health Programme was launched during 2014–15. DGHS describes strengthening public health facilities for accessible, affordable and quality oral health care. A programme objective is not proof that every local facility already meets it. Distinguish intended service improvement from verified outcomes when interpreting a government programme description.
units.question: Which aim matches the official NOHP description?
choices: Strengthen accessible, affordable, quality oral health care
Guarantee every candidate a government job
Publish unofficial exam weightage
units.explanation: NOHP concerns public oral health service delivery.
rationales: This matches the stated programme purpose.
Recruitment guarantees are not its purpose.
It does not establish exam weightage.

units.title: Quality has several dimensions
units.lesson: WHO identifies effective, safe, people-centred, timely, equitable, integrated and efficient services. Speed alone is therefore not a complete measure of quality. Measures should reflect the service context and be supported by accurate data. A quality-improvement claim needs observed evidence rather than only a statement of intent.
units.question: Which set consists of WHO service-quality dimensions?
choices: Only speed and advertising
Only activity counts and building size
Safe, effective and people-centred
units.explanation: These three are among WHO’s quality dimensions.
rationales: Advertising is not one of these care dimensions.
Inputs and activity alone are not the named dimensions.
This matches the framework.

units.title: Verify the exact recruitment case
units.lesson: UPSC recruitment requirements belong to the exact advertisement, post and any later corrigenda or test notices. A generic BDS topic map is not an official UPSC syllabus or weightage table. Check the official portal and recruitment case before treating a date, eligibility rule or assessment scheme as confirmed. This chapter does not claim a current Dental Surgeon vacancy or exam date.
units.question: Where should a claimed change to recruitment rules be checked?
choices: A forwarded screenshot alone
The relevant official UPSC notice and corrigenda
An invented app countdown
units.explanation: The issuing authority’s exact notice is the traceable source.
rationales: A screenshot may lack context or updates.
This is the appropriate official source.
An app cannot invent an official date.
units.hint: Follow the issuing authority and exact case.
